channel.title: MisaNeco Works Blog
channel.description: Practical, source-checked guides to automating admin for small businesses in the US, UK, Canada and Australia.

item.title: How to calculate forex position size from your stop-loss (formula and worked examples)
item.description: The position size formula for forex in plain English — amount at risk divided by stop distance times pip value — with worked examples for EUR/USD, USD/JPY and a non-USD account, how spread changes the result, and a free calculator.

item.title: Project end dates in Excel with WORKDAY.INTL — and the start-date gotcha that shifts every schedule by a day
item.description: How to calculate a job's finish date in working days with WORKDAY.INTL, count working days with NETWORKDAYS.INTL, set custom weekends and holidays, and avoid the most common mistake — WORKDAY.INTL does not count the start date itself.

item.title: Stop typos in your spreadsheet: make a drop-down list with Data Validation (Excel and Google Sheets)
item.description: The quickest way to stop typing mistakes in a business spreadsheet is a drop-down list. Step-by-step for Excel on Windows and Mac and for Google Sheets, how to keep the list in one place, what happens when someone types something else, and how to find entries that don't match.

item.title: Password rules for a small business: what NIST SP 800-63B-4 (2025) actually says
item.description: A plain-English summary of the password rules in NIST SP 800-63B-4 (final, July 2025) — minimum length, no forced complexity, no scheduled resets, blocklists, password managers — and a short policy a small business can copy.

item.title: How to calculate prorated rent (3 methods, with Excel formulas)
item.description: Prorated rent for a move-in or move-out month, explained with the three common methods (days in the month, a 30-day month, a 365-day year), worked examples, Excel and Google Sheets formulas, and what to check in your lease.

item.title: PHP critical RCE (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619): how to check your site and update
item.description: On 21 October 2026 PHP released fixes for two critical remote code execution flaws (CVSS v4.0 9.2). The fixed versions, who is at risk, how to check your PHP version on WordPress, shared hosting and your own server, and why php.ini changes are not enough — based on the official PHP advisory.

item.title: How to number your invoices (a simple system, plus a formula that does it for you)
item.description: A simple invoice numbering system for freelancers and small businesses (year plus a running number, like 2026-001), why it works, a formula that numbers invoices automatically in Excel or Google Sheets, and what to do about cancelled or corrected invoices. UK rules checked against GOV.UK.

item.title: How to work out the business-use share of home costs in a spreadsheet (US and UK)
item.description: A simple Excel or Google Sheets layout for splitting rent, utilities, phone and internet between business and personal use, plus the flat-rate options from the IRS and HMRC to compare against.

item.title: How to find reused and weak passwords (and which ones to fix first)
item.description: A short guide for small businesses and freelancers: use your browser's built-in Password Checkup to find compromised, reused and weak passwords, decide what to fix first, and handle an exported password file safely.

item.title: When someone leaves: an account offboarding checklist for small businesses
item.description: What to switch off, change, collect and record on the day an employee, part-timer or contractor leaves a small business, with a copyable checklist. Based on Japan's IPA security guideline for SMEs (version 4.0, March 2026).

item.title: Clicked a phishing link at work? What to do next (small business checklist)
item.description: Someone on your team clicked a link in a suspicious email, or typed a password into a fake login page. What to do next, step by step, based on the UK National Cyber Security Centre's phishing guidance, with a short checklist for small businesses.

item.title: Paying freelancers in the US - Form W-9, Form 1099-NEC and a simple tracking sheet
item.description: A plain-English guide for small US businesses that pay contractors. When to ask for a Form W-9, what Form 1099-NEC reports, the current threshold and deadline, and a spreadsheet layout that keeps January stress-free.

item.title: Track unpaid invoices in Google Sheets (with overdue days and red rows)
item.description: A simple invoice tracker that counts days overdue, colours late invoices red, and shows only the ones you need to chase. Works in Excel too, plus a polite reminder email you can copy.

item.title: Build a weekly staff shift schedule in Google Sheets (hours per person, gaps highlighted)
item.description: A weekly rota with shift codes, automatic hours per person, red cells when a shift is short of staff, and a view-only link for your team. Formulas also work in Excel.

item.title: Simple job costing in a spreadsheet - see if each job actually made money (Excel or Google Sheets)
item.description: Log materials, labour and subcontractor costs against each job, total them with SUMIFS, and see profit and margin per job. Low-margin jobs light up on their own. Works in Excel and Google Sheets.

item.title: Save Gmail attachments to Google Drive automatically (free Apps Script)
item.description: Label an email in Gmail and its attachments are saved to a Google Drive folder within the hour. A short Google Apps Script, one label, one trigger. No add-ons.

item.title: How to raise your prices as a small service business - a simple calculation and a customer letter template
item.description: Check your margin, model a price rise for each regular customer in Excel or Google Sheets, and tell customers with a short, clear letter. Includes two email templates and a checklist.

item.title: A simple quote-to-job tracker for trades and service businesses (Excel or Google Sheets)
item.description: Track every quote you send, see which ones need a follow-up call today, and work out your win rate with one COUNTIFS formula. Works in Excel and Google Sheets.

item.title: A simple monthly expense tracker in Google Sheets or Excel (with SUMIFS totals)
item.description: Log receipts, pick a category from a dropdown, and see spending by month and category with SUMIFS. Includes a missing-receipt check and a file naming tip. Works in Excel and Google Sheets.

item.title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - who must join, when, and a simple spreadsheet checklist
item.description: A plain-English guide to Making Tax Digital for Income Tax for UK sole traders and landlords. Who must join and when, what digital records and quarterly updates mean, and a spreadsheet setup you can copy.

item.title: A simple inventory tracker with low-stock alerts (Excel or Google Sheets)
item.description: Log stock in and out, let SUMIFS work out what you have on the shelf, and turn items red when they hit their reorder point. Works in Excel and Google Sheets, plus an optional Apps Script email alert.

item.title: A simple customer follow-up sheet (CRM-lite) for small service businesses
item.description: Track last contact and next action for every customer, see who is due today, spot customers who have gone quiet, and count your pipeline with COUNTIFS. Works in Excel and Google Sheets.

item.title: What a GST/HST invoice must show in Canada - a checklist and invoice template layout
item.description: The information the CRA says an invoice needs so your customers can claim input tax credits, by sale amount (under $100, $100 to $499.99, $500 or more), plus a checklist and a simple invoice layout for small businesses.

item.title: Admin automation for plumbers, electricians and builders
item.description: Nine small-business admin jobs for trades, from quotes to invoices, each with what is tedious, a few simple ways to fix it and a first step.

item.title: Simple automation for a small hair or beauty salon
item.description: Seven small admin jobs a salon or barbershop can simplify with tools it already has: booking, client records, rebooking, stock, takings, rota and replies.

item.title: How long to keep business records in the US, UK, Canada and Australia (and a simple filing system)
item.description: The official record-keeping periods for small businesses in four countries, checked against IRS, HMRC, CRA and ATO pages, plus a folder and file-naming system that makes old receipts easy to find.

item.title: Clean up a messy customer list in Excel or Google Sheets (5 formulas, 10 minutes)
item.description: Extra spaces, random capital letters, duplicate customers and mixed phone formats. Five simple formulas and two built-in tools fix most of it, in Excel and in Google Sheets.

item.title: How to Automate Invoicing and Payment Follow-Up
item.description: Automate invoicing and payment reminders step by step with a spreadsheet, email templates and bank files, with notes for the US, UK, Canada and Australia.

item.title: Send appointment reminder emails automatically with Google Sheets (free, no add-ons)
item.description: A short Google Apps Script that emails each customer the day before their appointment, using a simple Google Sheet. Copy, paste, set one trigger, done.
